questions.question: Order −6, 14, −2 and 3 from smallest to largest and explain how you compared −6 and −2.
questions.expected_answer: −6, −2, 3, 14. On the number line −2 is to the right of −6 (two below zero is warmer than six below), so −2 > −6.

questions.question: Count backwards in threes from 7 to −8 and forwards in fives from −20 to 5.
How much does the temperature rise from −6 °C to 3 °C? Explain using a number line.
questions.expected_answer: Counting up from −6 to 0 is 6 steps and from 0 to 3 is 3 steps, so it rises by 9 degrees.
